title: Qal'at al-Bahrain settlement
description: A fortified harbour town on the north shore began a mound of settlement layers that lasted four thousand years, thought to be the heart of Dilmun.

title: Islam reaches Bahrain
description: The ruler of Bahrain answered a letter sent by Muhammad, and his people were counted among the first converts outside Arabia proper.

title: Qarmatians seize Bahrain
description: The Qarmatians, a radical Ismaili movement, built a state in eastern Arabia that made Bahrain rich on pilgrimage tolls and raids for a century.

title: Portuguese take Bahrain
description: Antonio Correia's Portuguese squadron conquered the islands, raising the fort that still stands, and ruled through local clients for eighty years.

title: Persians take Bahrain
description: Shah Abbas I expelled the Portuguese, and Bahrain passed under Persian suzerainty for most of the next two centuries.

title: Al Khalifa take Bahrain
place: Zubarah to Manama attack route (shown at Manama)
description: The Utub clans of the Al Khalifa family conquered the islands from the Persian governor, founding the dynasty that still rules.

title: Truce with Britain
description: The Al Khalifa ruler signed a perpetual truce of peace and friendship, the first of a series of engagements binding Bahrain to Britain.

title: Exclusive Agreement with Britain
description: The ruler pledged not to deal with any power but Britain without consent, making Bahrain a British protectorate in all but name.

title: Oil discovered
description: The first oil well on the Arab side of the Gulf struck oil, starting the region's modern oil economy just as pearl diving collapsed.

title: Independence
description: As British forces left the Gulf, Bahrain declared independence under Emir Isa bin Salman, having four months earlier declined union with the other trucial states.

title: Constitution and National Assembly
description: A constitution took effect and men elected a National Assembly, dissolved by the emir two years later.

title: Coup attempt
description: Security services foiled a plot by the Iran-backed Islamic Front for the Liberation of Bahrain, deepening sectarian suspicion.

title: Uprising begins
description: Petition campaigns for restoring parliament turned into five years of unrest, marked by protests, arrests and deaths on both sides.

title: Hamad becomes emir
description: Hamad bin Isa succeeded his father Isa bin Salman after a reign of thirty-eight years and moved towards constitutional reform.

title: National Action Charter approved
description: Voters endorsed by 98 per cent a charter promising a constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament, ending the unrest of the nineties.

title: Kingdom of Bahrain declared
description: Hamad took the title of king as the emirate became a kingdom with a partly elected parliament.

title: Pearl Roundabout uprising
description: Protests for political reform filled the roundabout and were dispersed with deaths, and a month later a Saudi-led force helped clear the streets; the monument was demolished.

title: Dilmun burial mounds listed by UNESCO
description: Tens of thousands of Bronze Age burial mounds in the interior, raised by the Dilmun civilisation, were inscribed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
